lessons.body: Two pointers turn a search over pairs into a sequence of informed decisions. On a sorted array, increasing the left pointer increases the candidate sum; decreasing the right pointer decreases it. That monotonic relationship is what makes discarding candidates safe.

lessons.title: A little less work, every time

lessons.body: Suppose you need the largest sum of three consecutive values. You could add every group from scratch. But adjacent windows share almost everything. Keep a running sum: add the value entering from the right, then remove the value leaving from the left.

lessons.body: A queue preserves arrival order. Enqueue at the back and dequeue at the front. It is the natural structure when earlier work must be processed before newer work, such as breadth-first search.

lessons.title: Try a choice. Then undo it.
lessons.subtitle: Backtracking
lessons.body: Backtracking explores a decision tree while keeping only the current partial solution. In subset generation, choose a value, recursively explore what follows, then undo that choice before trying a different branch.
